name: hover-card
purpose: Rich preview that appears beside a link or name when the pointer rests on it or keyboard focus reaches it, and goes away when both leave. The root `HoverCard` owns the open state, the open and close delays and positioning (the shared `usePlacement`, the same engine as `Popover`); `HoverCard.Trigger` wraps the element being previewed; `HoverCard.Content` is the floating card. It sits between `Tooltip` (one line of plain text) and `Popover` (opened by a click, holds interactive content): the card shows a few lines of supplementary context, such as a person, a resource or a commit, without asking for a click.
useWhen: Use HoverCard for a read-only rich preview (a definition, a user card, a link preview) shown on hover or focus; interactive content is a Popover and a one-line hint is a Tooltip.
Previewing what a link points to before following it: a user handle in an audit log, a resource name in a table, a commit hash.
Showing a summary (status, owner, last update) that the destination page also shows.
avoidWhen: A one-line label or hint for an icon → use `tooltip`.
Content the user must act on (buttons, forms) or must be able to reach by touch → use `popover`.
The only place a piece of information appears. Hover and focus are not available everywhere; the card must repeat what the destination already shows.
related: `tooltip` — plain-text hint, same hover-and-focus model, no rich content.
`popover` — click-opened panel with focus management for interactive content; same positioning.
bestPractices: Wrap a link or a button: the trigger must be focusable on its own so keyboard users get the card too.
Keep the card to a heading line, two or three facts and at most one secondary link; it is a preview, not a page.
Keep the default delays (500 ms to open, 300 ms to close) so the card does not flash while the pointer crosses a list; shorten `openDelay` only for a single, deliberate target.
The pointer can move from the trigger onto the card without closing it, so a link inside the card is reachable; `Esc` closes it.

props.name: placement
props.doc: Side of the trigger the card opens on, flipped when it does not fit; `'auto'` picks the side with room.

props.name: offset
props.doc: Pixel gap between the trigger and the card.

props.name: openDelay
props.doc: Milliseconds the pointer or focus must stay on the trigger before the card opens.

props.name: closeDelay
props.doc: Milliseconds after the pointer or focus leaves the trigger and the card before the card closes.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.doc: Initial open state while `v-model:open` is unbound.
